$note: BOOKS CONFIG (no coding needed). One entry per book; books.html reads this file and renders the shelf, the search box and every exam / subject filter from it. Fields: id (url slug), title, author, publisher, edition, language (array), subject (an id from data/subjects.json), exams (exam ids or free tags), difficulty (Beginner | Intermediate | Advanced), rating (0-5, half steps), why (what the book actually covers - factual, one or two sentences), bestFor (who gets value from it), buyIf, skipIf (who should spend their money elsewhere), reread (how to use it across a preparation, not a claim about anyone's past), related (internal links a reader should go to next), url (purchase link - replace the Amazon search URL with an affiliate link by pasting it here; the button already carries rel=sponsored). Keep 'why' honest and specific: no superlatives, no guarantees, no invented pass rates.

books.title: Lucent's General Knowledge
books.author: Dr. Binay Karna, Sanjiv Kumar, Manohar Pandey
books.subject: gk
books.why: One compact book covering Indian history, polity, geography, economy and general science in point form, which is what a first read of the GK syllabus needs.
books.bestFor: Aspirants building a GK base from zero, and anyone revising facts the week before a paper.
books.buyIf: You want one affordable book that covers the static half of the GK syllabus end to end.
books.skipIf: You already maintain your own static GK notes - this adds nothing new.
books.reread: Read the sections that map to your syllabus once for coverage, then only the highlighted facts on later passes.

books.title: Objective General English
books.author: S.P. Bakshi
books.subject: english
books.why: Objective exercises on grammar, usage, error detection, sentence correction and comprehension, arranged topic by topic with answer keys.
books.bestFor: Anyone whose English marks are lost to grammar rules rather than vocabulary.
books.buyIf: You want graded practice questions after every rule instead of reading grammar passively.
books.skipIf: You are strong in English already - attempt the free sets here first and buy only if a gap shows.
books.reread: Work one topic at a time, mark every wrong answer, and return only to the topics you got wrong.

books.title: Quantitative Aptitude
books.author: R.S. Aggarwal
books.subject: quant
books.why: The standard reference for arithmetic and elementary mathematics, with theory, solved examples and a large graded exercise set per chapter.
books.bestFor: Building method in percentage, profit and loss, time and work, and the other arithmetic chapters that carry the paper.
books.buyIf: You need worked examples to understand a method before you can practise it.
books.skipIf: Your weakness is speed rather than concept - a mock series will serve you better.
books.reread: Read a chapter, solve only the exercise questions you got wrong the first time, and revisit them before every mock.

books.title: Fast Track Objective Arithmetic
books.author: Rajesh Verma
books.subject: quant
books.why: Shorter than the standard reference and organised around speed: each chapter gives the shortcut route to an answer alongside the long one.
books.bestFor: Anyone who already knows the concepts and now has to finish the arithmetic section inside the time limit.
books.buyIf: Your problem is time, not understanding.
books.skipIf: You are still learning the underlying methods - start with the standard reference instead.
books.reread: Use it as a revision book: one chapter, then timed sets of twenty questions.

books.title: A Modern Approach to Verbal & Non-Verbal Reasoning
books.author: R.S. Aggarwal
books.subject: reasoning
books.why: Covers the full reasoning syllabus - series, coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, syllogisms and non-verbal figures - with solved examples per pattern.
books.bestFor: Reasoning is usually the fastest section to fix: this book shows the pattern behind every question type.
books.buyIf: You can solve familiar questions but freeze when the pattern changes.
books.skipIf: You already clear reasoning comfortably in timed mocks.
books.reread: Learn one pattern, drill twenty questions of it, and move on - do not re-read the theory.

books.title: Indian Polity
books.author: M. Laxmikanth
books.subject: gk
books.why: The full constitutional framework: union and state executive, legislature, judiciary, panchayati raj and emergency provisions, explained chapter by chapter.
books.bestFor: Punjab PCS, UPSC and CAPF aspirants who need polity explained rather than summarised.
books.buyIf: Polity questions keep catching you between two similar-sounding articles.
books.skipIf: You are attempting only a constable-level paper - the GK reference covers what you need.
books.reread: Read a chapter once, then revise only the summary tables before each exam.

books.title: Lucent's General Science
books.author: Lucent Editorial Team
books.subject: gk
books.why: Physics, chemistry and biology at the level a general paper actually asks them, written in short facts rather than textbook prose.
books.bestFor: Non-science students who lose marks in the science portion of the GK paper.
books.buyIf: You need the science syllabus compressed into facts you can revise in a day.
books.skipIf: You have a science background and already score well here.
books.reread: Use it purely for revision: one pass before the exam, marking only what you did not know.

books.title: Wren & Martin's High School English Grammar & Composition
books.author: P.C. Wren, H. Martin
books.subject: english
books.why: The reference grammar behind the objective exercises: tenses, clauses, prepositions and modification explained with worked sentences.
books.bestFor: Anyone who keeps getting the same grammar rule wrong and needs the rule itself, not another question.
books.buyIf: You want to understand English rather than memorise answer patterns.
books.skipIf: You only need exam-shaped practice - the objective title beside it does that in less space.
books.reread: Pick the four or five chapters your mistakes point to and read only those.

books.title: Objective Computer Awareness
books.author: Arihant Experts
books.subject: computer
books.why: Objective coverage of fundamentals, hardware, software, operating systems, MS Office, internet, networking and cyber security with a practice set per chapter.
books.bestFor: Computer as a scoring section in Punjab Police, PSSSB and banking papers where the questions stay factual.
books.buyIf: You want the whole computer syllabus in question form.
books.skipIf: Your exam does not carry a computer section.
books.reread: Read once, then attempt the free computer sets here - revisit only the answers you miss.

books.title: India Year Book
books.author: Publications Division, Government of India
books.subject: current-affairs
books.why: The government's own record of the year: schemes, ministries, statistics and the state of the union, written by the departments responsible for them.
books.bestFor: PCS and UPSC aspirants who want the official version of a scheme rather than a magazine's summary.
books.buyIf: You are preparing for a state or civil services paper that asks about schemes and governance.
books.skipIf: You only need the month's headlines - the free current affairs section here covers that.
books.reread: Do not read it cover to cover: index the topics your syllabus names and read only those entries.

books.title: Pratiyogita Darpan
books.author: Upkar Prakashan
books.subject: current-affairs
books.why: A monthly magazine of current affairs with facts arranged for recall, plus practice questions at the end of each issue.
books.bestFor: Candidates who want current affairs in a form they can revise rather than re-read.
books.buyIf: You prefer one monthly book over tracking the news yourself every day.
books.skipIf: You already follow a daily source - adding a second one usually costs time, not marks.
books.reread: Read the issue when it arrives, then revisit only its question set the month after.

books.title: Punjab GK study material
books.author: House of Aspirants
books.subject: gk
books.why: Punjab history, culture, literature, geography and economy organised into five categories, in Punjabi and English, with a practice set under every chapter.
books.bestFor: Every Punjab exam, where state-specific questions are the section most candidates under-prepare.
books.buyIf: Nothing to buy - this is the free material on this site.
books.skipIf: Nobody. Start with the category you are weakest in.
books.reread: One category at a time: read the notes, attempt the set, then return to that category after two days.
